abstracts.value: Testing General Relativity (GR) on cosmological scales requires probes that are directly sensitive to gravitational dynamics. We present a Fisher matrix forecast of how well the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS) can constrain departures from GR through the cluster infall velocity field, using the redshift-space cluster-galaxy cross-correlation function $ξ^{\rm s}_{\rm cg}(r_p, r_π)$ as the primary observable. We construct mock catalogs from the AbacusSummit N-body simulations, using a Halo Occupation Distribution (HOD) model for galaxies and a log-normal mass-observable relation for cluster selection. We parameterize departures from GR with a single multiplicative factor $F_{\rm G}$ that rescales halo infall velocities relative to the GR prediction. Marginalizing over the HOD, mass-observable, and cosmological parameters, we find that DESI BGS can constrain $F_{\rm G}$ to $σ(F_{\rm G}) = 0.033$ at $z \sim 0.3$. This precision is sufficient to distinguish representative $f(R)$ and Galileon gravity models from GR at $\gtrsim 4σ$. The strongest limitation is a degeneracy between $F_{\rm G}$ and the scatter in the cluster mass-observable relation, while the constraint shows no strong degeneracy with any individual HOD parameter. Perfect knowledge of the galaxy-halo connection would improve the constraint to $σ(F_{\rm G}) \approx 0.015$, and including the galaxy autocorrelation function in the data vector could recover part of this improvement. The same data vector yields tight constraints on the cosmological parameters, $σ(Ω_m) = 0.010$ and $σ(σ_8) = 0.010$, only moderately correlated with $F_{\rm G}$. These results demonstrate the potential of DESI BGS cluster-galaxy correlations to test gravity on quasi-linear scales, complementary to existing modified gravity probes and to weak-lensing cluster mass profiles.

titles.title: The Redshift-Space Cluster-Galaxy Cross-Correlation as a Probe of Gravity on Cosmic Scales

abstracts.value: Relativistic heavy-ion collisions exhibit several phenomena commonly associated with the formation of a thermalized quark--gluon plasma. However, the observation of similar phenomena in small systems, and their non-thermal microscopic descriptions there, raises questions about this assumption. Recent continuum-extrapolated lattice-QCD calculations of the second- and fourth-order electric-charge susceptibilities, $χ_{2}^{ΔQ}$ and $χ_{4}^{ΔQ}$, reveal a striking tension with hadron-resonance-gas expectations, particularly for $χ_{4}^{ΔQ}$. As the ratio $χ_{4}^{ΔQ}/χ_{2}^{ΔQ}$ is experimentally measurable with net-charge cumulants, this opens up completely new ways to test whether thermal QCD applies in central heavy-ion collisions. However, achieving a measurement that can be interpreted with high precision requires further work on both the phenomenological and experimental sides. Here, the focus is on an experimental counterpart to recent phenomenological work on the $D$-measure of net-charge fluctuations: how restricted detector acceptance in rapidity and transverse momentum can be controlled experimentally. We demonstrate this for the second-order net-charge cumulant, $κ_2(ΔQ)$, by rewriting it in terms of the charge balance function and the charged-particle rapidity density. Both are event-averaged observables for which experimental efficiency corrections and extrapolations into unmeasured kinematic regions can be studied systematically. This provides a complementary experimental route for connecting measurements of $D = 4κ_2(ΔQ)/\langle N_{ch} \rangle$ to theory and a possible starting point for extending the same strategy to the fourth-order cumulant.

titles.title: Testing thermal equilibrium in heavy-ion collisions with electric-charge fluctuations

abstracts.value: Diffusion models are increasingly used as surrogates for expensive cosmological simulations, but simple metrics like reconstruction fidelity do not guarantee a surrogate can be trusted for scientific inference. To explore this, we train diffusion models on HI fields from the CAMELS IllustrisTNG simulations and test how three properties change with training-set size: memorization of individual training examples, agreement with one- and two-point statistics (the pixel-value distribution and the power spectrum), and estimation of cosmological parameters from the generated fields. At fixed model size, generative models trained with smaller, less diverse training data produced memorized samples. While this is a well known phenomenon, we show that this leads to miscalibrated parameter densities for cosmological inference tasks. At fixed size, there is a training set size with enough information content to enable a model to generalize, at which point posterior density estimation with neural surrogates can be well-calibrated. We demonstrate that a neural surrogate can therefore pass visual, one-point and power-spectrum convergence tests while still resulting in overconfident parameter estimation in a cosmological inference pipeline. Thus, tests of model generalization should be an additional check for inference pipelines adopting neural surrogates.

titles.title: Probing Cosmology with Diffusion Models: Memorization, Generalization, and Parameter Estimation

abstracts.value: The High-Luminosity upgrade of the Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC) will drastically increase the number of simultaneously interacting particles, posing a severe challenge to current particle reconstruction methods. While next-generation highly granular calorimeters offer unprecedented 3D measurement capabilities, reconstructing particles from heavily overlapping energy showers remains computationally difficult. This study investigates how raw detector hits can be accurately reconstructed using end-to-end transformer based methods on a simulated calorimeter dataset. We evaluate and compare three distinct machine learning frameworks, focusing on two generative architectures: diffusion and flow matching as well as query-based set prediction. Our results demonstrate that these advanced methods provide highly effective and scalable alternatives for resolving complex overlapping particle showers in conditions encountered in future calorimeters.

titles.title: End-to-end Particle Reconstruction with Transformers in High-Granularity Calorimeters

abstracts.value: We study the gravothermal collapse of inelastic dark matter halos with velocity-dependent elastic and dissipative self-interactions. Within the gravothermal fluid framework, we derive the effective cooling rate for dark matter upscattering to an excited state followed by decay back to the ground state, with emitted states carrying off energy from the halo. We solve the gravothermal fluid equations numerically to simulate spherically symmetric halos over the core-growing and collapse phases of their evolution. While halos with purely elastic self-interactions have universal evolution trajectories, inelastic dark matter halos exhibit much more diversity in their evolution. Nevertheless, inelastic halo dynamics contain a hidden parametric universality from which we derive a semi-analytic formula for calculating the halo collapse time for arbitrary velocity-dependent elastic and inelastic cross sections without the need for simulations.

titles.title: Core-collapse universality for inelastic self-interacting dark matter halos

abstracts.value: An accurate description of axion strings and their radiation is crucial for understanding their cosmological implications. Motivated by the differing conclusions of previous works, we study a simple, controlled setup: the collapse of an initially static circular loop in a Minkowski background. We compare field-theory simulations of the conventional complex scalar and high-tension Klaer--Moore models with solutions of the renormalised Nambu--Goto--Kalb--Ramond (NGKR) equation of motion, covering the range $3 \lesssim \mathcal{T} \lesssim 100$ in dimensionless string tension. Both the field theory and NGKR approach the Nambu--Goto (NG) limit with corrections scaling as $1/\mathcal{T}$. However, the leading correction to the halving-time is $20-35\%$ larger in NGKR than in the field-theory simulations over the same range of tensions, while for large tensions the value agrees with an independent perturbative calculation to $0.2\%$. The late-time axion spectrum agrees with NGKR in the infrared, but the collapse generates additional structure in the ultraviolet part of the spectrum, which we attribute to different events such as an outgoing wave front that carries a sizable fraction of the energy or the rebound of the initial loop. These results provide a useful benchmark for a more accurate understanding of axion radiation from cosmological string networks.

titles.title: Circular Axion String Loop Simulations: Field Theory and Effective Description

abstracts.value: Givens rotations with angles stored in quantum registers account for much of the cost of published quantum phase estimation algorithms based on double-factorized tensor hypercontraction and spectral amplification. These rotations create superpositions and cannot be verified directly by the basis-state evaluators used to optimize classical reversible circuits. We give an exact verification method that separates out a fixed Clifford change of basis and tracks basis states and phases in the remaining circuit. Integer conditions establish correctness of the full coherent action, including measurement-based uncomputation and restoration of the phase-gradient resource state. Under our interpretation of Low et al.'s angle grid and rotation convention, simplifying the adders lowers the rotation cost relative to the published accounting; fusing the two additions into one masked addition gives an additional saving. We verify both implementations exhaustively at every precision used in the published walks and prove the fused circuit correct for all widths. For benchmarks including FeMoco and other iron-sulfur clusters, replacing only the rotation term lowers total phase-estimation Toffoli counts by 9.5-14.3% under the published error budget, with the walk operator unchanged.

titles.title: Exact verification of Givens rotation circuits for efficient quantum phase estimation of iron-sulfur clusters

abstracts.value: We investigate whether interacting dark energy can provide additional relief to the Hubble tension once early dark energy (EDE) is present. Considering a cosmology containing EDE, an independent late-time dark energy fluid with an equation of state fixed at $w\simeq-1$ interacting with cold dark matter, and a cosmological constant, we find that the data strongly drive the model toward the non-interacting limit. The best fit effectively reduces to the standard EDE cosmology, where a non-zero EDE component provides most of the required increase in $H_0$, leaving little statistical gain for the interaction. Although energy transfer from dark matter to dark energy can raise $H_0$ further, this limited gain is rapidly outweighed by the deterioration of the fit to low-redshift observations. In particular, since the CMB tightly constrains the early-time physical matter density, any additional energy transfer requires a lower present-day matter abundance. Such low values are strongly disfavored by Type Ia supernovae. We show that this limitation becomes particularly severe once EDE has already raised $H_0$ and that the same mechanism extends to a broad class of post-recombination interactions. Allowing a dynamical dark energy equation of state of the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder form does not alter our conclusions.

titles.title: Early Dark Energy Crowds Out Interacting Dark Energy

abstracts.value: With D. Aerts, we showed in 2014, within the extended Bloch representation of quantum mechanics, that the Born rule can be understood as resulting from a universal average over all the possible ways in which the measurement-interactions can be selected. The cellular construction used there was since questioned, in the context of Bertrand's paradox, by N. Shackel, who observed that the result depends on the discretization adopted, that the sequence of averages is constant, and that the sense in which the average is taken over "all" densities remains unclear. Taking these criticisms as a stimulus, we re-examine the notion. The key is to recognize that a universal measurement is a random way of selecting a measurement which does not privilege any portion of the structure describing the available interactions, a property we call indifference. We prove that every indifferent universal measurement, however constructed, produces exactly the Born probabilities: the universal average is unique, and the cellular construction of 2014 is one among infinitely many ways of obtaining it, exact at every finite resolution. Non-trivial indifferent universal measurements exist, but must involve deterministic measurements: Dirichlet processes are indifferent universal measurements reaching every way of selecting an interaction, whereas an indifferent universal measurement free of deterministic components necessarily selects the uniform density, so that the Born rule holds not only on average but with certainty. Deviations from the quantum statistics in sequences of measurements are governed by a single parameter, in principle accessible to experiment. The only geometric inputs are the Euclidean length of the membrane and the orthogonal landing of the point-particle on it; the latter is where the content of Gleason's theorem lies. Generalizations to N outcomes and to Bertrand's paradox are discussed.

titles.title: Are quantum measurements universal?

abstracts.value: The Pusey--Barrett--Rudolph (PBR) theorem is commonly taken to establish that a pure quantum state represents a physical property of the system to which it is assigned, rather than merely encoding knowledge. In this work, I distinguish between state-first and dynamics-first physical theories, and argue that this reading presupposes the former. These two types of theories support different approaches to causal explanation, and one of PBR's stated assumptions depends on the state-first approach. Using a recent interpretation of quantum theory as a concrete example, I show how a dynamics-first theory can explain the PBR correlations while maintaining a broadly epistemic reading of quantum states. I conclude that the PBR theorem supports a dilemma: either the quantum state is part of reality, or reality is not fundamentally built out of states.

abstracts.value: We study the thermodynamics of quadrupolar Bose-Einstein condensates in the realm of the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) for the quest of understanding and testing quantum gravity (QG). Using both quadratic GUP (QGUP) and linear-quadratic GUP (LQGUP) which incorporate modified density of states, we calculate corrections to the condensed fraction, critical temperature, equation of state and other thermodynamic quantities. We find that the intriguing interplay of quadrupole-quadrupole interactions (QQIs) and the GUP may strongly modify the finite-temperature properties of the condensate, with the LQGUP generally predicting larger corrections than the QGUP, although their relative magnitudes depend on the chosen parameters and the validity of the perturbative expansion. We further estimate the sensitivity of the critical temperature to GUP-induced effects by imposing an assumed fractional temperature resolution which provides projected upper bounds on the GUP deformation parameters. Our findings demonstrate that quadrupole-quadrupole interacting Bose gases provide a promising platform for testing GUP-induced deviations from standard quantum mechanics and for probing QG phenomenology through measurements of finite-temperature many-body observables. They also motivate future studies using realistic system-specific parameters.

titles.title: Quantum gravity phenomenology in quadrupolar Bose-Einstein condensates: Finite-temperature thermodynamics and projected bounds

abstracts.value: We introduce a new, independent modeling component to the Carousel Lens series by exploiting the spatially-resolved kinematics contained within the lensed arcs, which so far has remained rather underexplored in strong-lensing analyses. We present an end-to-end forward-modeling framework that reconstructs an integral-field spectroscopic datacube from a parameterization of the lens convergence profile together with the line-of-sight velocity, velocity dispersion, and surface brightness profiles of the unlensed source. The kinematic structure of the source acts as an additional set of ray-traceable markers distributed across every lensed image, inaccessible from imaging data alone. Furthermore, by generating an [OII] emission-line datacube, we isolate a single source redshift and remove lens and line-of-sight light contamination. We apply this framework to deep VLT/MUSE observations of the Carousel Lens, modeling the [OII] emission of the quadruply-imaged star-forming galaxy at $z_{\rm s} = 1.432$ that anchors the system's cosmography constraints. We measure an Einstein radius $θ_{\rm E} = 12.816''^{+0.005}_{-0.007}$ and a logarithmic slope $γ= 1.412^{+0.002}_{-0.002}$, tightening the statistical uncertainties on both by roughly a factor of $2-2.5$ relative to the corresponding flat emission-line map model. We find that the source galaxy exhibits a strong rotation, lies confidently along the star-forming main sequence, and has an inferred central black hole mass of $\log M_{\rm BH}/M_{\odot} = 7.89 \pm 0.51$. These results establish datacube-level forward modeling as a practical and independent route to traditional image-based lens models in the current systematics-limited regime, and one that extends naturally to this system's other lensed sources and to other lens systems.

titles.title: The Carousel Lens III: Joint lens convergence and source kinematic modeling

abstracts.value: We develop an inverse-design approach to the effective field theory (EFT) of perturbations in scalar-tensor gravity around static and spherically symmetric backgrounds with a timelike scalar-field gradient, taking the odd-parity effective potential as input and reconstructing compatible background and EFT data. As analytically tractable examples, we construct explicit realizations of the Pöschl-Teller potential, for which the quasinormal-mode spectrum can be obtained in closed form. We then study the Regge-Wheeler potential of general relativity and its parametrized deformations, showing how both can be realized within the scalar-tensor EFT. In particular, the latter realizations provide a route to interpreting phenomenological constraints on potential deformations from black hole ringdown observations in terms of the underlying EFT data.

titles.title: Inverse design of scalar-tensor EFT from odd-parity effective potentials

abstracts.value: Binary neutron star (BNS) mergers are among the primary sites of the rapid neutron-capture (r-)process. In mergers with long-lived remnants, sustained neutrino irradiation raises the electron fraction of the disc wind ejecta, modifying the resulting nucleosynthesis pattern. Yields from numerical-relativity simulations with accurate neutrino transport are needed to quantify the contribution of BNS mergers to the Galactic production of heavy elements and to interpret kilonova spectra. We present and publicly release tracer trajectories and nucleosynthesis yields for eight BNS mergers forming long-lived neutron star remnants, obtained from general-relativistic simulations with M1 neutrino transport, spanning two equations of state (DD2 and SFHo), and a range of total masses and mass ratios. Passive tracer particles following the dynamical and wind ejecta were post-processed with the nuclear reaction network WinNet up to 1 Gyr. The yields and tracer trajectories are available on the MARTINI platform. At 1 day, the production of light and first-peak elements (He, Ni, Sr, and Y) is similar across models and is primarily enhanced by the neutrino-irradiated disc wind. The yields of heavy nuclei vary by more than one order of magnitude, with unequal-mass binaries producing the largest amounts owing to their more neutron-rich ejecta. Our He yields, particularly in the wind, exceed those of recent studies based on an M0 neutrino scheme, consistent with the stronger neutrino irradiation resulting from an M1 scheme. At 1 Gyr, all models reproduce the second and third solar r-process peaks, but differ in the first peak, the lanthanide region, the mass range between the first and second peaks, and the trans-lead region, reflecting the electron fraction distribution of the ejecta and the dynamical and wind contributions. Two equal-mass models provide a close match to the solar pattern.

titles.title: The MARTINI platform II. Tracing r-process nucleosynthesis in neutron star mergers with long-lived remnants

abstracts.value: We study the decay $ψ(3686)\to p K^- \bar K^0 \barΞ^0$, treating the $ψ(3686)$ as a $c\bar c$ state and therefore as a singlet under SU(3) transformations in the light-quark sector. We consider all possible combinations of a baryon, an antibaryon, and two pseudoscalar mesons that form an SU(3) singlet, retaining the terms that can lead to the $p K^- \bar K^0 \barΞ^0$ final state through $S$-wave final-state interactions. Three independent SU(3)-singlet structures are identified and assigned different weights. We also include the contribution of the $Λ(1520)$ in the meson-baryon $D$-wave. A fit to the data provides a good description of all six invariant-mass distributions. In addition to the $Λ(1520)$ contribution, we find a small contribution from the $Λ(1670)$ in the $K^-p$ invariant-mass distribution, generated by final-state interactions, and a contribution from the $Σ(1430)$, which produces a significant distortion of the $\bar K^0p$ invariant-mass distribution relative to phase space. This study demonstrates the value of investigating charmonium decays into a baryon-antibaryon pair and two pseudoscalar mesons, complementing the more commonly studied decays into a baryon-antibaryon pair and a single pseudoscalar meson.

titles.title: Meson-baryon final-state interactions in the $ψ(3686)\to pK^-K_S^0\barΞ^0$ decay

abstracts.value: We study the charged Breitenlohner--Freedman (BF) bound for all horizon harmonics of the type IIB $t^+$ Kaluza--Klein tower on extremal charged AdS$_5$ black holes with equal rotations. The scalar equation follows from maximal five-dimensional gauged supergravity at level zero and the linearized exceptional-field-theory equations at higher levels. For aligned charge and rotation, a quadratic form in charge and spin changes signature on the curve of supersymmetric (BPS) black holes, where every mode satisfies the bound. Above the curve, where $Ω_H>1$, every black hole has a violating mode, although no finite truncation in level or spin detects violation at every such black hole. Below the curve, where $Φ_H>1$, the BF-passing set is confined to a thin strip and controlled by charge and spin discreteness. At large radius and fixed rotation, a level-four mode with spin proportional to the radius violates the bound even where all U(2) singlets satisfy it. These results concern the near-horizon BF bound of one tower in two-derivative supergravity; full radial stability remains open.

titles.title: Near-horizon BF bounds for the $t^+$ KK tower on extremal AdS$_5$ black holes

abstracts.value: Context. Blazars are the main population of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) detected in gamma rays by Fermi. However, around 34% of Fermi sources remain unidentified, partly due to their large positional uncertainties, motivating multiwavelength methods to identify possible counterparts. Aims. We evaluate a method proposed to identify BL Lacertae (BL Lac) candidates among unidentified Fermi sources based on their X-ray properties, using Swift-XRT observations. Methods. We examined published optical spectra for an initial sample of 148 X-ray-selected candidates. We found 71 sources with spectra spatially consistent with the proposed associations and reassessed their classifications using standard blazar criteria. We then compared these classifications with the method's initial predictions. Results. Of the 71 proposed counterparts, 80.28% are classified as BL Lac objects and 87.32% as possible gamma-ray-emitting AGNs, supporting the effectiveness of the X-ray-based selection. We also identify four Seyfert galaxies, suggesting that the method is sensitive to this class despite its rarity among gamma-ray emitters. Conclusions. Our results show that X-ray observations are effective for selecting BL Lac candidates among unidentified Fermi sources and support future spectroscopic follow-up campaigns. The high fraction of BL Lacs and AGNs suggests that blazars may account for a substantial part of the unidentified gamma-ray population. The Seyfert identifications also raise questions about the origin of high-energy emission in AGNs not typically associated with relativistic jets, highlighting the need for further multiwavelength observations.

titles.title: Validating an X-ray-based method for identifying Fermi blazars

abstracts.value: Five years ago Pook-Kolb, Hennigar and Booth published a series of three papers exploring the evolution of apparent horizons and other marginally outer trapped surfaces during a black hole merger. This was seen to be much more intricate than the well-known "pair-of-pants" merger associated with event horizons. In this paper we show that parameter evolutions of Brill-Lindquist-deSitter initial data mimic many of the features of that evolution. Hence, this analytic intial data is a useful testing ground for ideas about marginally outer trapped surface evolution and spacetime geometry during mergers.

titles.title: Apparent horizon mergers in analytic intial data

abstracts.value: We provide a detailed resource estimate of the state-of-the-art sum-of-squares block encoding algorithm for electronic structure Hamiltonians of Low et al. on superconducting cat qubits. To achieve this, we present compilations with closed-form costs of the dominant subroutines such as skew-tree Qrom, a Swap network and a Phaseup for both a repetition-cat and an LDPC-cat architecture. Our compilation represents algorithmic qubits in the $X$ basis, taking advantage of the asymmetric cost of $X$ and $Z$ access that the concatenation of cat qubits with phase-flip classical code brings. Additionally, we provide a protocol for $\vert i \rangle$-state distillation and a two-level Toffoli-like $\vert \text{C}_X\text{C}_X X \rangle$ magic state distillation protocol, including three factory layouts. To minimize the cost of Clifford corrections induced by magic state injections we tailor injection gadgets to each subroutine. Combining our compilation work with the adder compilation from the companion work Pappalardo et al., we provide global layouts for the block encoding in both architectures which we use to obtain resource estimates for ground-state energy estimation for the benchmarks of FeMoco-54 and FeMoco-76. Assuming a cycle time of 1$μ$s, a reaction time of 10$\mathrmμ$s, a phase estimation precision of 1 mHa and circuit-level phase-flip noise with probability $p_Z = 5 \times 10^{-4}$ with negligible bit-flip error, FeMoco-54 requires fewer than $7\,500$ cat qubits with an expected runtime of under one day for a single phase estimation run using an LDPC-cat architecture. Relaxing the bit-flip requirement to $p_X = 10^{-11}$ with an additional layer of elevator codes raises this to an estimated $13\,000$ cat qubits.

titles.title: Ground-state energy estimation compiled on cat qubits: 7 164 qubits for FeMoco-54 in 23.5 hours

abstracts.value: Hodoscopes consisting of triangular counters with embedded wavelength shifting fibers are becoming more popular as they are relatively inexpensive, are easily fabricated, need no cooling systems, employ low-cost photodetectors, require only modest voltages, and perhaps most importantly, have good position resolution. Through interpolation of the light yields between adjacent counters, position resolutions that are typically an order of magnitude better than the counter separation can be obtained. Here, after a brief explanation of how the interpolation is done to improve the position resolution, we derive an approximate expressions for the uncertainty in the interpolated $x$ and $y$ positions as a function of the impact position of the charged particle.

titles.title: The Position Resolution of a Charged Particle Hodoscope Consisting of Triangular Scintillator Counters

abstracts.value: Continuous variable quantum key distribution enables two parties to extract provably secure keys for cryptography by exploiting aspects of quantum mechanics. A central challenge in achieving QKD over long distances is overcoming optical loss, which limits the secret key rates and achievable transmission distances. Recent work has illustrated how to perform continuous variable quantum key distribution while eliminating information leakage to an eavesdropper in a pure-loss channel and minimizing information leakage in a noisy channel. In this work, we analyse this protocol under conditions where the quantum channel linking the sender and receiver is a fading channel, which can be used to model free-space links. We find that the protocol maintains strong performance over fading channels and outperforms comparable protocols.

titles.title: Continuous variable quantum key distribution through a fading channel with minimal information leakage

abstracts.value: PSR J0835-4510 (a.k.a. the Vela pulsar) is the best studied pulsar in the Southern hemisphere given its high radio brightness and large glitch activity. However, its X-ray brightness is comparatively lower, making the study of its X-ray profile difficult. We aim to investigate the X-ray emission of the Vela pulsar coming from the surface of the neutron star to infer the properties of its hotspots and assess whether they share a common spectral shape. We also aim to prove whether the 2021 glitch affected the hotspots. We used ephemeris obtained from high-cadence radio observations with the radio telescopes of the Argentine Institute of Radio Astronomy to combine all the NICER observations of the Vela pulsar after its 2019 glitch and before its 2024 glitch. We obtained a folded pulse profile for three different energy ranges and subsequently studied their phase-resolved energy spectra. We additionally analyzed a Chandra observation to quantify the pulsar's contribution to the total soft X-ray emission detected by NICER, which cannot spatially resolve the pulsar from the surrounding pulsar wind nebula (PWN). The pulsar contribution to the total observed emission represents less than 40-45% of the flux below 0.9 keV, dropping to 3-4% in the 0.9-2.0 keV range and further down to ~2% above 2 keV, where the PWN fully dominates. We find that the X-ray folded profile of the Vela pulsar was not measurably perturbed by the 2021 glitch. We studied separately seven regions of the pulse profile. We found that all of them are well modeled by one or two blackbodies. The temperatures of these hotspots are between $0.79(7) \times 10^{6}$ K $\leq T \leq 4.8^{+0.8}_{-0.6} \times 10^{6}$ K, while their sizes vary between $0.048^{+0.016}_{-0.009}$ km $\leq R \leq 3.9^{+0.9}_{-0.6}$ km, and their luminosities between $5\times10^{30}$ erg/s $\lesssim L < 1\times10^{32}$ erg/s.

titles.title: Phase-resolved X-ray spectroscopy of the Vela pulsar with NICER observations

abstracts.value: Braiding Majorana zero modes does not by itself provide a universal set of quantum gates. Additional operations can be supplied through ancillary states, whose preparation need not have the same protection as braiding. Here, we consider purification of the non-Gaussian ancilla used for an entangling gate in Bravyi's scheme. We keep his elementary braid-and-fusion comparison and change how its outputs are combined. An additional layer compares the product of the three stabilizer signs. The first accepted errors giving an incorrect output then require three faulty input blocks rather than two. As a result, the preparation error decreases cubically instead of quadratically, and the asymptotic raw-copy overhead is reduced. We also construct a preliminary sequence in which a processed block is paired with a fresh copy from the same noisy source. For independent inputs supported in the even-parity sector and ideal purification operations, this sequence establishes a sufficient distillability fidelity of 59.95 percent after free Gaussian twirling. At a common source fidelity, it reduces the expected cost of preparing an input for the recurrence by more than seven orders of magnitude relative to the balanced construction studied here. Finally, we examine imperfect purification operations in an effective syndrome-noise model. The additional layer leaves the leading operation-error coefficient unchanged, although a nonzero error floor remains.

titles.title: Reducing the cost of ancilla purification for Majorana quantum computation

abstracts.value: AI coding agents are extremely effective at performing calculations that can be broken down into modular steps, each with verifiable checks of correctness. Perturbative QCD calculations satisfy both of these properties and we find that they are well-suited to solution by agentic AI systems. We discuss our methods for instructing and verifying the work of agents in one- and two-loop perturbative calculations, with a focus on pre-empting common mistakes. We find that once an agent has successfully completed one perturbative calculation, its instructions transfer very well to other similar calculations which can then be completed and verified in a matter of hours with little effort from the user.

titles.title: Agentic AI for QCD perturbation theory or: how I learned to stop worrying and love the bot

abstracts.value: The observation of orbital eccentricity in compact binary coalescences would provide a direct signature of dynamical formation environments. Previous matched-filter searches for eccentric neutron star-black hole (NSBH) binaries have been severely limited by computational constraints, necessitating the use of simplified waveform models that capture secular dephasing but omit apsidal precession and inter-orbit harmonics. Including these physical features increases the sensitive search volume for systems with $0.2 \le e_{20} \le 0.28$ by $\sim 25\%$ to $30\%$. We present a rapid matched-filter search methodology that makes the direct use of time-domain effective-one-body waveforms computationally feasible. By multibanding and high-frequency ratio-filtering, our pipeline achieves a $\sim 20\times$ reduction in computational cost. This allows a bank of 88.6 million effective-one-body templates, fifteen times larger than prior eccentric analyses, to search O4a and O4b Advanced LIGO data. We recover the known low-mass mergers GW230518_125908 and GW230529_181500 with parameters consistent with zero eccentricity. Finding no new gravitational-wave events with orbital eccentricity ($e_{20} \ge 0.05$), we place $90\%$ credible upper limits on the local merger rate density of eccentric NSBH systems across the search space of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 7.5\text{-}57\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, up to a factor of $\sim 4$ improvement over previous observational bounds. At the parameters of GW200105_162426, this non-detection establishes an upper limit of $\mathcal{R}_{90\%} \le 12.1\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Alternatively, if GW200105_162426 is treated as an eccentric detection, the lack of subsequent detections in O4 updates the inferred local merger rate density of this population to $\mathcal{R} = 6.6^{+6.3}_{-3.8}\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.

titles.title: Search for Eccentric Neutron Star-Black Hole Binaries in Advanced LIGO's Fourth Observing Run using Effective-One-Body Waveforms

abstracts.value: Baryon-number-violating decays with missing energy probe new interactions connecting Standard-Model quarks to light invisible fermions. Such signatures can arise from dimension-six operators coupling three quarks to an SM-singlet fermion $χ$, which escapes detection. With a suitable baryon-number assignment for $χ$, total baryon number is conserved while its violation is apparent in the visible sector. We study the exclusive decays $Λ_c\toπ\barχ$ and $Λ_c\to K\barχ$, determining the required form factors using light-cone sum rules with pion and kaon distribution amplitudes. The calculation includes leading-order two-particle contributions up to twist four and factorisable four-particle terms. Two $Λ_c$ interpolating currents are employed to assess the current dependence. Using single-operator benchmarks based on collider bounds, we obtain branching fractions of order $10^{-7}$ over sizeable parts of the physical region, with uncertainty envelopes reaching $10^{-6}$ in some scenarios. These are indicative estimates within the retained light-cone expansion. We compare with existing chiral-perturbation-theory and QCD-factorisation estimates and discuss experimental prospects. Future data from STCF and Belle II could probe part of the predicted range, while FCC-ee could reach smaller branching fractions.

titles.title: Baryon-Number Violating $Λ_c$ Decays from Light-Cone Sum Rules

abstracts.value: Generative learning of a quantum measurement distribution from finite data requires choosing a model capacity that balances representation accuracy against estimation cost. We develop a bias-variance framework that decomposes the expected population Kullback-Leibler error at model capacity $s$ and sample size $N$ as $\mathcal E(s,N)=B(s)+V(s,N)$, with representation bias $B$ and a variance term $V$ capturing the mean estimation error. In the well-sampled regime, $V(s,N)\simeq[NC(s)]^{-1}$, and exponential or algebraic laws for $B$ and $C$ yield four scaling templates for the optimal error, from inverse powers of $N$ to inverse powers of $\ln N$. For local autoregressive models, the context radius sets the model capacity, and $B$ is the summed conditional mutual information lost by truncating the context. For a smoothed histogram learner, we derive an exact finite-sample estimation cost that accounts for rarely observed contexts and recovers the parameter-count law in the well-sampled regime. For transverse-field Ising Born distributions, the independently evaluated bias and estimation cost predict both the optimal context radius and the optimal error. In the well-sampled regime, the estimation cost grows exponentially with context radius. Its competition with approximately exponential bias decay in the gapped regimes predicts power-law error decay in $N$, while algebraic bias decay at criticality predicts asymptotic inverse-power decay in $\ln N$. Bulk-site results are consistent with the corresponding finite-sample predictions. These results connect the structure of quantum measurement distributions to the model capacity justified by finite data.

titles.title: Sample Complexity for Generative Learning of Quantum Measurement Data

abstracts.value: We present an end-to-end resource estimation of Shor's algorithm on superconducting cat qubits, from its mathematical description to the allocation and scheduling of physical qubits on a chip layout. We review modern versions of Shor's algorithm for RSA, ECDLP and FFDLP, and make their logical circuits and trade-offs explicit. We compile the dominant subroutines down to physical-qubit operations on two architectures: one based on repetition cat codes and one on LDPC cat codes. We design a parity-Cnot gate for cat qubits, extend a multi-target Cnot gate to the LDPC-cat architecture, and adapt an active injection procedure to cat qubits. Building on these primitives, we adapt to cat qubits the adder from Gidney's 2025 resource estimate for factoring RSA-2048. We combine our adder compilation and a coarser estimate for the phaseup with the factory designs and lookup compilation from the FeMoco resource estimation of Kroell et al. Together, these lead to chip layouts and schedules for factoring RSA-2048. Assuming a 1$μ$s error-correction cycle time, a 10$μ$s reaction time, circuit-level phase-flip noise with probability $p_Z = 5 \times 10^{-4}$ and no bit-flips, factoring RSA-2048, the configuration we compile in full, requires about 23 000 cat qubits and 3.14 days. Reusing the compiled operations, solving ECDLP on secp256k1 requires at most 30 000 cat qubits and 1 hour, and FFDLP-512, which we propose as an intermediate benchmark, about 6 700 cat qubits and 21 minutes. Trading space for time, RSA-2048 runs in 1.25 hours on about 611 000 cat qubits. The no-bit-flip requirement (a bit-flip time of about 100 years) can be relaxed to a bit-flip time of about one hour by adding a concatenation layer with a distance-3 bit-flip code, in which case RSA-2048 needs about 45 000 cat qubits.

titles.title: Shor's algorithm compiled on cat qubits: 22 593 qubits for RSA-2048 in 3.14 days

abstracts.value: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. Photoluminescence excitation reveals higher excited states, enabling coherent control of trion transitions and the observation of Rabi-like oscillations in both telecom bands. These results confirm the promising potential of these quantum dots for applications in quantum technologies.

titles.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs

abstracts.value: Quantitative studies of laser-driven ion acceleration and laser-induced nuclear fusion require accurate measurements of ion yields and energy spectra. Although scintillator screens integrated with Thomson parabola spectrometers provide real-time diagnostics, their nonlinear scintillation response requires absolute calibration. We present an in situ, single-shot cross-calibration method using a 2-mm-period CR-39 sampling mask to simultaneously record particle counts and scintillation signals from laser-accelerated proton beams. The method is applied to calibrate a 400-$μ$m-thick CsI:Tl crystal and a 6-$μ$m-thick P43 phosphor screen over a broad proton energy range. The measured scintillation responses are compared with a theoretical model combining Birks' law and simulated proton stopping powers. The calibration quantitatively reveals the distinct response characteristics of the two scintillators, including thickness-dependent punch-through effects and constraints on ionization quenching, and demonstrates a practical approach for the absolute calibration of scintillator screens used in laser-driven ion spectroscopy.

titles.title: Absolute calibration of scintillators for laser-driven ion spectroscopy using in situ CR-39 sampling detectors

abstracts.value: Galactic foregrounds present a major challenge for cosmic microwave background (CMB) cosmology as their amplitudes exceed the target primordial $B$-mode signal. While small-scale interstellar medium (ISM) emission is expected to be highly complex, current foreground simulations cannot reproduce the filamentary, non-Gaussian features of ISM structure in a stochastic way. To address this gap, we introduce a framework for generating stochastic small-scale foreground emission, using polarized synchrotron observations as an example use case. This method is capable of producing many independent realizations that additionally inherit morphological information from large angular scales. The underlying structural complexity incorporates anisotropic, multifractal, and advected non-Gaussian features that are tunable with a small number of parameters that carry physical interpretations. Because standard power spectra do not describe the complex phase coherence required for the structural complexity, we evaluate the synthetic fields using higher-order statistics, demonstrating that the Minkowski functionals and structure functions partially capture varying degrees of non-Gaussianity. This work lays the necessary foundation for new foreground simulation suites with stochastic realizations of possible non-Gaussian structure.

titles.title: Simulating and Characterizing Non-Gaussian Small-Scale Polarized Emission

abstracts.value: The positive-P representation for bosons allows scalable exact simulations of many-body open quantum systems, provided dissipation is strong enough to stabilise stochastic trajectories. Designing analogous methods for spin systems, relevant to quantum technologies, remains challenging, as previous spin positive-P formulations can exhibit systematic errors even when simulations are numerically stable. Here, we develop a phase-space representation that maps spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ degrees of freedom onto parameters of a local generalized density matrix (GDM), rather than SU(2) coherent states. In all stable regimes, we observe no deviations from exact solutions, restoring the positive-P property: stable solutions are exact up to stochastic sampling noise. The GDM representation combines seamlessly with bosonic positive-P, enabling highly scalable treatment of coupled spin-boson systems. We map simulation stability versus spin and boson dissipation in the Jaynes-Cummings model and apply the method to a Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard quasi-Lieb lattice, showing how spin dissipation and driving can destroy or restore excitation incompressibility.

titles.title: Exact Positive-P Simulation of Open Quantum Spin Systems with Generalized Density Matrix Formalism

abstracts.value: We present measurements of the scale of cosmic homogeneity using the first data release (DR1) of the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI), the largest publicly available spectroscopic extragalactic survey to date. Using a counts-in-spheres estimator applied to nearly 5 million galaxies and quasars across six independent redshift bins spanning $0.1 < z < 2.1$, we measure the correlation dimension $D_2(r)$ and define the homogeneity scale $R_H$ as the point at which the galaxy distribution reaches within 1% of the homogeneous asymptotic value. We find that all tracers clearly transition to homogeneity, with the galaxy homogeneity scale ranging from $93.8^{+0.9}_{-0.7}$ to $142.6^{+1.4}_{-1.4}$$h^{-1}$Mpc depending on the tracer redshift, galaxy bias, and modelling used to extract the scale. Using a cosmology-dependent model, we reconstruct the underlying matter homogeneity scale, finding it decreases monotonically with redshift in excellent agreement with $Λ$CDM predictions. We identify a systematic offset of up to $\sim 10\%$ between measurements in the North and South Galactic Caps, largely due to fiber assignment effects reproduced in our simulations. Accounting for this, and with a complementary demonstration using toy models that our methodology correctly identifies inhomogeneous universes in all but rather finely-tuned observer configurations, this hence provides strong evidence in favour of the cosmological principle across our full redshift range. Our matter homogeneity scale measurements are consistent with, and substantially more precise than, previous constraints from WiggleZ and SDSS, demonstrating the power of DESI data for precision tests of the cosmological principle.

titles.title: The scale of homogeneity in DESI Data Release 1

abstracts.value: Fermi-LAT observations imply that most of the cosmic rays (CRs) produced in normal star-forming galaxies escape from the discs where they are accelerated into the circumgalactic medium (CGM), but the subsequent evolution of those escaping CRs is unclear. Here we construct a simple semi-analytic model for their transport and loss, which we constrain by confronting the model with a series of observations: limits on CR energy densities in the outer Milky Way from Fermi-LAT, the isotropic gamma-ray background (IGRB), stacked CGM X-ray emission from eROSITA, and the requirement that the accumulated pressure of CRs in galaxy CGMs not be so large as to render them unstable. We show that these constraints can be jointly satisfied in only two scenarios: one where CRs diffuse quickly through the CGM and freely escape beyond it into the IGM, and another where the CR diffusion time out of halos is of order the Hubble time. In the latter scenario CRs accelerated by star formation naturally explain both the IGRB and the heat input required to maintain the temperature of the CGM against X-ray cooling, and their relatively slow transport means that roughly half of the CR energy injected into the CGM of an $L_\star$ halo over its star-formation history remains there at $z \simeq 0$. This makes CR pressure dynamically significant, and also means that a non-negligible part of the IGRB is produced by CRs in the Milky Way's own halo. We argue that this latter scenario is the more likely one, as it avoids the need to posit a second source for the IGRB that is coincidentally very close in both power and spectral shape to the contribution from star-forming discs.

titles.title: Cosmic rays in galaxy halos I: the circumgalactic transport rate and a dynamically significant cosmic-ray reservoir

abstracts.value: Quotient quiver subtraction translates the gauging of Coulomb branch global symmetries into a combinatoric operation on 3d $\mathcal{N}=4$ gauge theories. This work uses brane systems to introduce a systematic method to gauge $\textrm{U}(n)\times\textrm{U}(n')$ and $\textrm{SU}(n)\times\textrm{SU}(n')$ emergent Coulomb branch global symmetries. Similar to other recently-introduced techniques, the gauging operation is a two-step process; in this case, it involves the symplectisation of unitary gauge factors into symplectic groups. A host of explicit examples are used to verify the procedure, and connections are made to Class $\mathcal{S}$ theories and three-dimensional theories realising maximal implosion spaces.

titles.title: Quotient Quiver Subtraction -- Product Groups

abstracts.value: General relativity, a theory that is already over a century old, is still the best theory that we have to describe the universe at energy scales where only the gravitational force is important. It has stood tall to any observational tests thrown at it since its inception, and it has remarkable predictive power when it is utilized to study and model astrophysical problems. It also continues to surprise us with its ability to generate new problems and insights that render themselves useful in the study of modern physics. This is especially highlighted by the transition of modern observational astronomy away from an electromagnetic radiation epoch, and into a new gravitational wave epoch. This thesis devotes its study to phenomena that can be analyzed within the framework of classical general relativity, but whose results may contain interesting implications for cosmological and black hole observations. (Full abstract can be found in document).

titles.title: Physical Effects in the Vicinity of Black Holes

abstracts.value: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

titles.title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes

abstracts.value: Algebraic quantum field theory describes a quantum system through its observables, their localisation in spacetime, and the states that assign them expectation values. The separation of the specification of observables from the choice of a state makes it possible to compare vacuum, thermal and charged representations without assuming that they share a preferred Hilbert space. We develop the framework from familiar quantum mechanics, construct the free scalar field, and explain how causality and positive energy constrain local measurements. The Reeh--Schlieder theorem, the structure of local von Neumann algebras and the split property reveal key differences between quantum theory in the continuum (i.e. QFT) and ordinary quantum mechanics with finitely many degrees of freedom. Superselection theory relates observable charges to statistics and internal symmetries. Finally, local covariance and perturbative and homological methods extend the discussion to curved spacetime, interactions and gauge theories. We also discuss measurement theory and quantum information aspects of AQFT.

titles.title: Algebraic Quantum Field Theory

abstracts.value: We investigate a traversable Morris–Thorne wormhole supported by a Hernquist dark-matter halo, in which the Hernquist central density controls both the optical appearance and the scalar-wave scattering properties of the geometry. We show that two critical densities govern the photon-sphere structure and use them to compute the shadow radius and strong-deflection lensing coefficients. We further show that the central density drives a topological transition in the scalar effective potential, from a single throat-centered barrier to a symmetric double-barrier configuration. In the single-barrier regime, third-order WKB and direct time-domain evolution agree at the percent level, confirming linear mode stability with longer-lived, lower-frequency ringdown as central density increases. In the double-barrier regime, time-domain evolution reveals delayed, echo-like modulations whose separation scales with the cavity width, while real-frequency scattering calculations reveal narrow, multipole-dependent graybody resonances with near-unit transmission at selected frequencies. These results provide a unified optical and wave-scattering characterization of a two-ended, dark-matter-supported wormhole.

titles.title: Traversable wormholes in Hernquist dark matter halos: Photon spheres, quasinormal modes, and echo-like signatures

abstracts.value: Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy combining intense infrared and x-ray pulses is an important tool for investigating complex structural and electronic dynamics in materials. However, current configurations combining external sources and x-ray free-electron lasers (FELs) often suffer from high system complexity, inherent timing jitter, or limited pulse properties. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the generation of intrinsically synchronized soft x-ray (SXR) and midinfrared (MIR) FELs from a single prebunched electron beam. Sequentially passing the beam through an SXR undulator followed by an MIR amplifier reveals a highly synergistic process: the initial periodic MIR density modulation boosts the SXR FEL pulse energy, while robustly surviving the intense SXR FEL to drive high-power, narrowband MIR radiation. Extending this scheme to lower terahertz frequencies suppresses SXR power, but this can be compensated by machine tuning. Originating from the same electron bunch, the dual-color pulses inherently maintain a precise, constant time delay. This intrinsically synchronized scheme establishes a highly reliable platform tailored for both SXR-pump and infrared-probe and infrared-pump and SXR-probe experiments.

Ultrafast pump-probe spectroscopy combining intense terahertz (THz) and X-ray pulses is a critical tool for investigating complex structural and electronic dynamics in materials. However, current setups combining THz sources and X-ray free-electron lasers (FELs) often suffer from high system complexity, inherent timing jitter, or limited THz pulse properties. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the generation of intrinsically synchronized, strong-field, narrow-band THz and X-ray FELs from a single pre-bunched electron beam. Sequentially passing the beam through X-ray and THz amplifiers reveals a highly synergistic process: the initial periodic THz density modulation notably boosts the X-ray FEL pulse energy, while robustly surviving the intense X-ray emission to drive high-power, narrow-band THz radiation. Originating from the same electron bunch, the two pulses inherently maintain a precise, constant time delay. This jitter-free scheme establishes a highly reliable platform tailored for both X-ray-pump/THz-probe and THz-pump/X-ray-probe experiments.

1. Introduction

A strong enough external electric field can produce pairs of charged particles from
vacuum. This non-perturbative phenomenon in quantum field theory, that was
originally proposed by Sauter [31] and further investigated by Heisenberg and
Euler [18], is known as the Schwinger effect after the work of Schwinger [32] in
which a complete theoretical description is given (see, e.g., [10] for a recent review).
With a uniform background electric field E in flat spacetime, the number density
(probability) of the created pairs is proportional to the factor exp

(
−πm2/eE

)
,

where m and e are the particle mass and charge (coupling), respectively. This
pocket formula shows that the pair production occurs when the electric field is
as strong enough as a critical field Ecr ≃ m2/e; otherwise it is exponentially
suppressed. For the lightest charged particle, the electron, we need an intense
field Ecr ≃ 1.3× 1018 V/m [6] that is still experimentally far-reaching. This is the
main obstacle to directly observe the Schwinger pair production in ground-based
experiments. Nevertheless, as pointed out in the review article [30], one could
search for the imprint of the Schwinger effect in astrophysical and cosmological
contexts where extremely intense background fields could naturally be present.
This could be done, e.g., by considering the backreaction of the created pairs or
the signature of the induced current on the magnetogenesis and inflation.

De Sitter (dS) geometry plays a crucial role in our current understanding of
cosmology. Specifically, the inflationary background in the early universe (see, e.g.,
[2, 22] for reviews) as well as the present day accelerated expansion of the universe
(see, e.g., [5] for review) is approximately described by dS spacetime. Widely
motivated from false vacuum decay and bubble nucleation to cosmological appli-
cations including magnetogenesis or giving a thermal interpretation, Schwinger
mechanism in dS background has been extensively studied for various types of
particles and spacetime dimensions [3, 4, 8, 9, 16, 17, 19, 21, 34, 36, 37]. Thanks
to the curvature of the spacetime, Schwinger pair creation mechanism in 1 + 1-
dimensional dS geometry showed some quite peculiar features [8, 9, 19, 36, 37].
In particular, in the case of light fields, the current induced by created particles
is inversely proportional to the applied electric field which leads to the so-called
infrared hyperconductivity. The analysis, extended to 1+3-dimensional dS space-
time, showed further unexpected results [16, 17, 21]. Furthermore, in [3], it is
shown that the Schwinger effect tends to have the similar aspects even in 1 + d-
dimensional dS background. However, it is claimed recently that the unintuitive
infrared behavior (negative conductivity) of the induced Schwinger current in dS
space might be an artifact of regularization schemes [1].

Most of the previous works assumed a uniform background electric field with
constant energy density to consider Schwinger effect in dS space, which is in con-
trast with the realistic situation. Indeed, the background electric field would be
changed due to the backreaction of the created pairs and the expansion of the
universe. More importantly, the constancy of the energy density violates the sec-
ond law of thermodynamics in the case of a homogeneous field configuration in an



Schwinger Pair Creation by a Time-Dependent Electric Field in dS4 37

expanding conformally flat background [12]. Recently, in some realistic models,
Schwinger pair production by time-dependent inflation-driven electric field and
its backreaction to the background geometry has been investigated [11, 20, 33].
These studies employ the fact that during the anisotropic inflation a persistent
electric field can be established by introducing a time-dependent gauge kinetic
coupling between the inflation and the gauge field [7, 39]. It is shown that, for
light charged scalar field, the pair production probability is strongly enhanced
in the weak electric field limit and the infrared hyperconductivity also occurs in
anisotropic inflation [11]. On the other hand, in the strong-field regime, it is shown
that the Schwinger current has the same functional dependence as in the case of
a constant electric field [20].

Unlike the case of flat space, studying the Schwinger effect in time-dependent
electric field background has been limited to some special cases in curved spacetime
(see, e.g., [14, 15, 23, 35, 38]). This is mainly because, in the presence of a time-
dependent background in curved spacetime, it is generally difficult to solve the
field’s equations of motion to find the mode functions and interpret them in terms
of positive- and negative-frequency modes. Thus, one needs either to choose a
special form for the scale factor or to restrict himself/herself to a particular time-
dependent electric field. Nevertheless, one can resort to approximate methods.
Based on Olver’s uniform asymptotic approximation method for the solution of
the second-order differential equation with two turning points [26], the Schwinger
effect coupled to inflation has been recently studied in [11] with the focus on the
weak electric field and light mass limits. In the present work, we use this uniform
asymptotic theory, that was developed further in [41, 42, 43, 44], to investigate the
Schwinger pair creation by a time-dependent electric field in de Sitter spacetime.
For different parameter region (different cases of the turning points), we compute
the pair production probability and study its different features. We show that the
pair creation is enhanced for light scalar fields, while is suppressed exponentially
for massive particles. We also compute the semi-classical electric current in the
weak electric field limit and show that the negative conductivity occurs.

The rest of the article is organized as follows. In Section 2, we first intro-
duce the setup (i.e., the background spacetime and the time-dependent electric
fields). Then, starting from the action, we obtain the equation of motion for a
charged scalar field in these backgrounds. We show that the problem of finding
the mode functions is reduced to solve a second-order differential equation which
does not admit an exact analytical solution. We briefly introduce the uniform
asymptotic approximation method in Section 3 and use it to find the approximate
mode functions. We use these approximate mode functions to define the “in” and
“out” vacuum states for the quantized scalar field, and compute the Bogoliubov
coefficients and pair production probability in Section 4. Then, we explore the
different features of the pair creation for the different parameter regions (that lead
to different natures for the turning points). Finally, we conclude in Section 5. The
appendix include some useful information on Weber’s equation, parabolic cylinder
functions and their asymptotic expansion.

5. Conclusion
In this work, we have investigated the Schwinger pair creation by a time-dependent
electric field in (1+3)-dimensional de Sitter spacetime. Specifically, in dS4, we
have considered a charged scalar field, as a test field, coupled to a time-dependent
background electric field (3) which has a time-dependent energy density in the
expanding universe. We have seen that, while the field equation of motion does
not admit an exact analytical solution, it can be solved by means of Olver’s uniform
asymptotic approximation method. We showed that the equation of motion, in
general, has two turning points, whose natures (single, double, real or complex)
depend on the value of the electric field E, the particle’s massm, and wave vector k.
Using the first-order approximate solutions (the mode functions for the canonical



56 F. Monemi and F. Zamani

quantization) the Bogoliubov coefficients and consequently the probability for the
pair production were computed both analytically and numerically, which strictly
depends on the natures of the turning points. More precisely, we found that
the pair creation process is enhanced when the two turning points are real and
single, and suppressed when they are complex conjugate. Furthermore, when the
particle’s mass and momentum are small, two turning points are real, and the
more smaller are the easier to create particles by the Schwinger mechanism. For
massive particles or large momentums, both turning points are complex, and the
Schwinger pair creation is exponentially suppressed. In addition, for both cases of
real and complex turning points, we explored that the modes with anti-screening
orientation (kz > 0) are different from those with screening orientation (kz < 0)
in pair production process. Indeed, light (massive) particles with anti-screening
orientations are hardest to be produced (are more suppressed) than those with
screening orientations.

For small particle’s mass and momentum, in the weak electric field limit, we
also computed analytically the pair production probability and the semi-classical
electric current induced by the created Schwinger pairs. Remarkably, we found
that the pair creation probability |βk±|2 and hence the semi-classical current J are
strongly enhanced as the electric field diminishes. Indeed, as E → 0, pair creation
probability and the semi-classical current diverge, respectively, as 1/E2∆+1 and
1/E2∆ (1− lnE), where ∆ :=

abstracts.value: Quantum software development is challenged by quantum-mechanical semantics and fragmented software development kits (SDKs), which complicate cross-SDK code translation and execution. In this paper, we propose an LLM-based approach for translating executable programs between high-level quantum SDKs. We develop a quantum-aware translation workflow whose prompt design and validation reflect quantum semantics and accommodate the version evolution of quantum ecosystems. We conduct a preliminary evaluation of 4 LLM configurations on 43 tasks, translating Qiskit programs to PennyLane and Q#. LLMs achieve a zero-shot Pass@1 of up to 72.33%, while one-shot prompting further improves the translation effectiveness. These results suggest potential for quantum code translation by LLMs.

titles.title: Large Language Models for Quantum Code Translation: An Exploratory Study

abstracts.value: Characterizing nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensembles requires connecting their collective spectra to individual centers that experience different local environments. We develop a symbolic-regression pipeline that carries single-center spin structure into a calibrated ensemble model by generating individual spectral responses and combining them with explicit weights. A constrained search selects Hermitian operator terms from single-center optically detected magnetic resonance spectra, fits their coefficients, and retains the selected expressions as source models for the ensemble. Ensemble calibration then accounts for resonance shifts, local disorder, orientation, and optical response while keeping the individual spectral contributions accessible. On public single-center and ensemble data, the zero-field ensemble held-frequency root-mean-square error decreases from 0.008835 to 0.003872 in normalized photoluminescence, a 56.2% improvement over matched uncorrected composition. In controlled QuTiP ensembles of 128 sites spanning four NV orientations, models calibrated at 0 and 3 mT predict an independently held-out 5.17 mT spectrum with errors of 0.000207-0.000228 across three random seeds, comparable to the 0.000200 noise standard deviation. Resolving the simulated response into its individual-center contributions shows how local spectral diversity combines into the ensemble line shape. By retaining the source Hamiltonians while calibrating sample-dependent spectral differences, the pipeline connects local spin physics to collective optical readout and makes the contributions to an ensemble line shape available for physical interpretation.

titles.title: From Single Spins to Ensembles: A Calibrated Symbolic Regression Pipeline for NV Spectroscopy

abstracts.value: For the quantum phase estimation (QPE) algorithm we study the minimal space of observables that is sufficient to predict the entire output distribution under open dynamics of the counting register. Building on the general Krylov theory of reduction, we compute the structure of this space explicitly for the full Fourier measurement. The outcome probabilities are determined by cyclic sums of the state matrix. If the adjoint generator is diagonal on the matrix units, the spectral classes inside the residue classes of the index difference modulo the register dimension $M$ give a constructive basis, an exact dimension formula, and attainable bounds: the dimension of the visible space lies between $M$ and $M^2-M+1$. The class includes independent qubit dephasing, and an analytically solvable reference model of Gorini--Kossakowski--Lindblad--Sudarshan (GKLS) type yields a damped Fejér kernel; two random-unitary channels with the same Ramsey contrast show that higher harmonics are distinguishable in the QPE distribution. For approximate reduction we use a finite-time Gramian and an a posteriori residual estimate, with a quadratic error order for a reducing unperturbed subspace and a compatible initial state. Numerical calculations check the consistency of the representations and the behaviour of the error under non-Toeplitz perturbations.

titles.title: Measurement-dependent reduction of open dynamics in the quantum phase estimation algorithm: the visible subspace and the damped Fejér kernel

abstracts.value: Factored gradient descent (FGD) is a scalable nonconvex method for low-rank positive semidefinite matrix recovery, in which the rank and positivity constraints are satisfied automatically by the factorization. Most of the existing theory that certifies benignity of its loss landscape, however, relies on a restricted isometry property (RIP) of the measurement map. In quantum state tomography, one of its applications, the measurements that can be acquired with stable statistics are limited by detection efficiency and drift to Pauli observables of low weight; we first show that under such partial-weight Pauli measurements RIP fails in the worst possible way. We then bundle the mutually commuting observables setting by setting, pushing the state forward to the probability distribution of each setting, and introduce a max-sliced total-variation loss. On the stratum where the setting attaining the maximum is unique there is no spurious local minimum, and provided only that the measurement map is injective on generic pure states, the global minimum is the truth up to a phase. Finally we verify these claims numerically on four qubits and compare against FGD with the ordinary loss.

titles.title: Rank-one Factored Gradient Descent without Restricted Isometry: Application to Quantum Pure State Tomography on Multi-Qubits

abstracts.value: We prove the $C^0$-inextendibility of the full Kerr realizations considered in this paper and all their connected covering spacetimes. The result holds for positive mass and nonzero rotation in the subextremal, extremal, and overextremal regimes. The obstruction at the singular ring is expressed by unbounded proper time in a fixed-endpoint causal homotopy class. It persists under every positive continuous conformal rescaling and under continuous widening of the Kerr causal cones, without any global causality assumption. We give sharp bounds in a fixed coordinate norm for stationary and axisymmetric perturbations and describe complete timelike geodesics that encounter arbitrarily large curvature near the ring.

titles.title: The $C^0$-inextendibility of Kerr spacetimes
